minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued the Chase Road, Mass Ave and DPW hearings to March 4 and set a Saturday site walk.
minutes.summary: The commission funded an Eagle Scout bat house project, heard the Chase Road common driveway and two-house filings, and took public comment on the Mass Ave earth removal. It held an enforcement hearing on an Allen Road lakefront property at Hickory Hills, extended a pond herbicide permit with added conditions, and approved minutes. Most hearings were continued pending DEP numbers, plan revisions or site visits.

public_comment.topic: Asked what a storm drain is and who will maintain the Mass Ave basin and how often.
MS4 warrant article this spring, who certifies vernal pools, and concern that subdividing the house lot would circumvent the zone three limit.
Worried about runoff, dust, flooding, property value and ledge near his backyard; said he received no notice.
Said it was ruled earlier that there would be no blasting.
Reported filling and clearing at the Allen Road lakefront and asked for remediation with native planting.
Pointed to the deed's 50 foot setback for structures.

Continue the three Chase Road hearings to March 4.
Continue the Mass Ave hearing to March 4.
Continue the DPW culvert hearing to March 4.
Continue the 51 Fire Road retaining wall hearing to March 4.
Hold a site walk on February 22 and keep the enforcement on the agenda.
Extend the herbicide order for three years with seven days' notice and an annual report.

budget_items.what_was_said: Estimate to build and mount four bat houses; the board would cover any shortfall from fundraising from its gift fund.
A landowners representative said treatment funding is significant for the association.

Site visit at the Allen Road property set for Saturday February 22, with Hickory Hills representatives invited.
Enforcement stays on the next agenda.
Agent to get an update on land acquisition for next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission continued the three Chase Road hearings, the Mass Ave earth removal hearing, the DPW culvert hearing and the 51 Fire Road hearing to March 4.
The commission set a site walk at the Allen Road lakefront property for Saturday, February 22, and kept the enforcement matter on the next agenda.
The commission extended the pond herbicide order for three years, with seven days' notice and an annual report.
The commission voted to fund an Eagle Scout bat house project from its gift fund, covering any shortfall from the project's fundraising.
A Chase Road site visit was set for Saturday, February 29, at 9:30.

why_it_matters: Chase Road, Mass Ave and the DPW culverts have no final decision yet, so neighbors worried about runoff, flooding or blasting can still be heard on March 4.
The herbicide extension and the Allen Road enforcement bear on how Hickory Hills' pond is treated and on the shoreline, and the association said the treatment cost is significant for it.
watch_next: March 4: continued hearings on Chase Road, Mass Ave, the DPW culverts and 51 Fire Road.
The next agenda: the Allen Road enforcement item, and the agent's update on land acquisition.
